title: Xin Dynasty
capsule: The Xin ('New') dynasty was the brief Chinese imperial state (9–23 AD) founded by Wang Mang, a Han chancellor who deposed the infant Han emperor and proclaimed himself Son of Heaven, claiming a mandate for institutional reform. Wang Mang enacted sweeping but unworkable reforms — nationalising land, abolishing slavery, and changing official titles — which alienated the landowning elite and failed to alleviate peasant poverty. A devastating Yellow River flood around 11 AD and the catastrophic Famine of 11–17 AD sparked the Red Eyebrow Rebellion and other uprisings; rebel forces captured the capital Chang'an in 23 AD and killed Wang Mang, ending the dynasty after only fourteen years. The Han dynasty was restored in 25 AD under Emperor Guangwu.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Xin dynasty mirrors the Western Han core and is well documented by Han administrative geography (commanderies and kingdoms); the effective loss of northern frontier zones to the Xiongnu during the dynasty's turmoil is attested textually but imprecisely mapped.
